_meta.name: Aircraft and helicopter parts
_meta.basis: HS 2022 nomenclature; Section XVII Note 2 (parts of general use, engines, electrical equipment, instruments and seats are classified in their own headings, not as aircraft parts); WCO Explanatory Notes to headings 88.02, 88.06 and 88.07.
_meta.rule: A part is classified under 8807 (parts of aircraft) only when it is identifiable as suitable solely or principally for aircraft AND it is not excluded by Section XVII Note 2. Note 2 sends fasteners, seals, springs, bearings, engines and their parts, pumps, valves, electrical equipment, instruments, lighting and seats to their own chapters, whatever they are fitted to. That is why a screw is a screw (73.18) even when it holds a helicopter together.
_meta.duty_note: Civil aircraft and most civil-aircraft parts are duty-free in the signatories of the WTO Agreement on Trade in Civil Aircraft (US column 'C' free; EU end-use relief under Regulation 2018/581 with an EASA Form 1 / FAA 8130-3; UK, Canada, Japan similar). Malaysia and Singapore charge 0% duty on 8802/8807; SST or GST still applies. Military aircraft parts, used/serviceable parts and dual-use items need export licences from the origin country.

confidence_legend.check: defensible but origin/destination rulings vary — confirm with a binding ruling or the airworthiness documents

items.n: Cockpit windshield or window of laminated safety glass
items.note: Glass specially shaped for aircraft is classified as glass (70.07), not as an aircraft part.

items.n: Cabin window pane of acrylic / stretched PMMA
items.note: Shaped aircraft windows of plastics are usually accepted in 8807.30; some administrations take 3926.90.

items.n: Nacelle, cowling, inlet or thrust reverser
Structural fitting, bracket or lug machined for one aircraft type
items.note: Only when identifiable as an aircraft part; a generic bracket of base metal is 7326.90 (steel) or 7616.99 (aluminium).
8512.40 covers wipers for motor vehicles only.

items.n: Tail rotor blade or tail rotor assembly
Rotor hub, rotor head, swashplate, pitch link, pitch horn, blade grip
Propeller, propeller blade, hub or spinner

items.note: Governor integral to the propeller system → 8807.10; a stand-alone speed governor can fall in 8481.80 or 9032.89.
Gearboxes not integral to the engine stay in Section XVII (Note 2(e) excludes 84.83 articles only when they are engine parts), so 8807.30 rather than 8483.40.

items.n: Tail rotor drive shaft, hanger bearing, flexible coupling
items.note: The ball or roller bearing inside a hanger bearing is 8482 on its own.
Clutches of 8483.60 are excluded only as integral engine parts; the helicopter freewheel sits between engine and gearbox.

items.n: Turbofan / turbojet engine, thrust up to 25 kN

items.n: Part of turbojet or turboprop: fan blade, compressor blade, turbine blade, disc, vane, combustor, nozzle guide vane, engine case, seal segment
Part of turboshaft / APU (same components, 'other gas turbine' parts)
Part of piston aero-engine: cylinder, piston, crankshaft, camshaft, valve

items.note: Ball bearings 8482.10; cylindrical roller 8482.50; tapered roller 8482.20 — always their own heading.

items.n: Engine fuel pump, oil pump, scavenge pump
items.note: 8413.30 is for internal-combustion piston engines; turbine engine fuel/oil pumps go to 8413.60 (rotary positive-displacement) or 8413.70 (centrifugal).
Pneumatic air-turbine starters are 8412.80 (other engines and motors).

items.n: Engine oil cooler / fuel-oil heat exchanger
items.note: Section XVII Note 2(e) keeps radiators for engines in the vehicle chapter; most administrations classify aircraft oil coolers as heat exchangers 8419.50.
Filters for piston engines: 8421.23.
Engine exhaust parts can also be taken as engine parts (8411.91/99); nozzle parts of the engine itself are 8411.

items.n: Landing gear leg, oleo strut, shock absorber, trunnion, drag brace, torque link

items.note: Hydraulic cylinders/actuators are 8412.21 (linear) or 8412.29 whatever they move.
